q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Survey Committee appointed in a stores depot?

options.A: Examining unserviceable stores placed before it
options.B: Passing suppliers' bills for payment after linking them with purchase orders
options.C: Recommending condemnation of stores found unfit for further use
options.D: Recommending the mode of disposal of stores surveyed off

q: A lot of scrap is sold by e-auction. The purchaser deposits the sale value, but delivery of the material has not yet been given to him; later, when the sale is finally adjusted, the sale value is found to differ from the book value of the scrap. The deposit awaiting delivery is held under ______, and the difference between the sale value and the book value is adjusted through ______.

options.A: Purchase Suspense — Sales Suspense
options.B: Sales Suspense — Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Stock Adjustment Account — Sales Suspense
options.D: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense — Purchase Suspense

q: A consignment of stores despatched by a supplier has arrived at the destination station, but the Railway Receipt for it has been lost in transit and has not reached the consignee depot. To avoid detention of the wagon, the depot can take delivery of the consignment by:

options.A: Furnishing an indemnity bond for the value of the consignment, undertaking to indemnify the Railway against claims in respect of it
options.B: Refusing to unload the wagon until the original Railway Receipt is found
options.C: Paying the full value of the stores again in cash to the station
options.D: Taking delivery only after a fresh purchase order is placed on the supplier

q: In inventory management, the approach under which rigorous control is exercised only over selected items — such as high-value items under ABC analysis and vital items under VED analysis — while the remaining items are controlled loosely, is known as:

options.A: Uniform control
options.B: Perpetual control
options.C: Periodic control
options.D: Selective inventory control

q: For ready location and correct identification of stores in a depot, every bin, rack or stack in the depot is provided with a label or tag which shows the:

options.A: Name of the supplier who last supplied the item
options.B: Price Ledger (PL) number and the nomenclature (description) of the item stocked there
options.C: Date on which the depot was last inspected
options.D: Total value of the stock held in the whole depot

q: A field official holding imprest stores applies for replenishment of the stores consumed by him, but he has not rendered any account of the consumption of the stores last supplied to him. The correct course is that replenishment is:

options.A: Made only after he renders the account of consumption of the stores already held by him, the replenishment being confined to the quantities so accounted for
options.B: Made in full at once, the account of consumption being called for afterwards
options.C: Refused permanently and his imprest is cancelled in all cases
options.D: Made by inviting fresh tenders for the quantities demanded by him

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 4,800 units. Coverage for three months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 500 units. The quantity required to be ordered is:

options.A: 1,200 units
options.B: 300 units
options.C: Nil, as the stock in hand and the dues together exceed the quantity needed for three months' coverage
options.D: 2,600 units

q: An imported stores item is invoiced at Rs 2,00,000. The freight paid on it is Rs 20,000, the insurance premium Rs 5,000 and the customs duty Rs 25,000. The value at which the item is taken into stock in the priced accounts (its landed cost) is:

A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 6 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 400 per day for the period of delay, as per the conditions of sale given to him. The ground rent payable by him is:

options.A: Rs 400

q: A purchase order is placed for 800 units of an item at Rs 150 per unit. The Railway later exercises the option clause in the order and calls for an additional quantity of 200 units on the same terms and rate. The value of the additional quantity supplied under the option clause is:

A stores contract containing a price variation clause stipulates that the price payable shall vary in proportion to a specified index named in the contract. The contract rate is Rs 500 per unit and the specified index rises from 100 to 110 during the currency of the contract. The revised rate payable per unit, worked out as stipulated in the contract, is:

options.A: Rs 550
options.B: Rs 510
options.C: Rs 500
options.D: Rs 605

q: In a stores tender, the lowest bid of Rs 4,00,000 is from a non-local supplier. A Class-I local supplier has bid Rs 4,70,000. The margin of purchase preference admissible to a Class-I local supplier under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order is 20 per cent of the lowest bid. The correct position is that the Class-I local supplier:

options.A: Cannot be considered at all, his bid being higher than the lowest bid
options.B: Must be given the order automatically at his own quoted rate of Rs 4,70,000
options.C: Is outside the margin of purchase preference, as 20 per cent of the lowest bid is only Rs 40,000
options.D: Is within the margin of purchase preference, the ceiling under the margin being Rs 4,80,000, and can be given the opportunity to match the lowest price of Rs 4,00,000

q: Which of the following measures will NOT help a railway to improve (lower) its Turnover Ratio of stores?

options.A: Disposing of dead surplus and obsolete stock lying in depots
options.B: Purchasing additional quantities of slow-moving stores for stocking in depots
options.C: Reducing the coverage prescribed for high-value stock items
options.D: Clearing long-outstanding suspense balances forming part of the stores balance

q: Which of the following is NOT a duty of the storekeeper (stockholder) in charge of a ward of a stores depot?

options.A: Safe custody of the stores held in his ward
options.B: Maintenance of bin cards showing quantities received, issued and in balance
options.C: Vetting of indents for procurement of stores to see that funds are available for the purchase
options.D: Producing the stores in his charge for stock verification when required

q: On agreement of the records of a depot, the folio of an item in the Priced Stores Ledger is found to show a credit (negative) balance, although stores of the item are physically present in the depot. This position primarily indicates that:

options.A: A receipt of the item has remained unposted, or an issue has been posted in excess, in the priced accounts, and the postings must be checked and rectified before any adjustment is made
options.B: The item has become obsolete and must be surveyed off at once
options.C: The stock verifier must write off the value of the item immediately
options.D: The book rate of the item should be increased to remove the negative balance

q: A Survey Committee examining stores in a depot finds a quantity of stores which the holding depot does not require, but which are in serviceable condition and are reported to be in regular use in another depot of the railway. The appropriate recommendation of the committee in respect of such stores is that they be:

options.A: Condemned and sold as scrap forthwith
options.B: Destroyed, as the holding depot has no use for them
options.C: Kept in the depot indefinitely without any entry
options.D: Transferred to the depot which requires them, instead of being condemned

q: Stores returned to a depot are classified as repairable, but on examination the cost of repairing a particular item is found to be so high in relation to the cost of a new item that repair is uneconomical. The correct course in respect of such an item is to:

options.A: Repair it regardless of the cost involved
options.B: Issue it to a consuming department in its unrepaired condition
options.C: Place it before the Survey Committee for condemnation and disposal as scrap
options.D: Retain it in stock permanently as a repairable item

q: A work returns to a stores depot a quantity of material which has been in use and has deteriorated. The returning work claims credit at the full rate at which the material was originally issued to it. The credit admissible to the work is:

options.A: At the full original issue rate, as claimed by the work
options.B: At the value assessed for the returned material in its present condition, and not at the original issue rate
options.C: At the current market price of new material of the same description
options.D: Nil, as no credit is ever given for material returned to stores

q: A depot requires a spare part for an imported machine, and the part is manufactured and supplied only by the original equipment manufacturer of the machine, no other source being available for it. The spare is correctly procured:

options.A: From the original equipment manufacturer as a proprietary item, on the basis of a Proprietary Article Certificate, through single tender
options.B: Only through an open tender advertised to all registered firms
options.C: By reverse auction among all the firms registered with the Railways
options.D: By local spot purchase from any dealer in the open market

q: A purchase order placed on a supplier is cancelled before any supply is made against it, but the quantity covered by the order continues to be shown in the depot's records as 'dues' while a fresh demand for the item is being covered. If this is not corrected, the effect is that:

options.A: The coverage of the item is understated and excess stock will be ordered
options.B: The book rate of the item will automatically increase
options.C: The cancelled order will revive and bind the supplier again
options.D: The coverage of the item is overstated, as quantities which will never be received are counted as forthcoming, and the fresh order quantity is correspondingly understated

q: In the records of a stores depot, the stock sheet and the bin card are maintained by two different functionaries. The correct pairing is:

options.A: Stock sheet — depot storekeeper; Bin card — stock verifier of the Accounts Department
options.B: Stock sheet — stock verifier of the Accounts Department, for recording differences found on verification; Bin card — depot storekeeper, for recording quantities at the bins
options.C: Stock sheet — supplier of the stores; Bin card — depot storekeeper
options.D: Stock sheet — depot storekeeper; Bin card — depot storekeeper

q: The stores organisation of a zonal railway works at two levels below the headquarters. The correct pairing of the level with the officer heading the stores organisation at that level is:

options.A: Division — Depot Materials Superintendent; Depot — Controller of Stores
options.B: Division — Senior Divisional Materials Manager; Depot — Depot Materials Superintendent
options.C: Division — Senior Divisional Accounts Officer; Depot — Senior Divisional Materials Manager
options.D: Division — Depot Materials Superintendent; Depot — Principal Chief Materials Manager

q: Materials are received at a stores depot against a purchase order in which inspection before acceptance is prescribed, but the materials are taken straight into the priced stock of the depot without any inspection being carried out. The correct position is that the materials should have been:

options.A: Kept apart, outside the priced stock, until they were inspected and accepted, and taken into stock only thereafter under a receipt note
options.B: Issued to the consuming department immediately, inspection being carried out after issue
options.C: Returned to the supplier in every case, even if they conform to the specification
options.D: Taken into stock at a reduced rate fixed by the storekeeper as a penalty for non-inspection

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a railway workshop for a manufacturing job, but the job is cancelled before the material is consumed and the material remains unused with the workshop. The correct treatment of the unused material is that it is:

options.A: Retained by the workshop indefinitely without any accounting entry
options.B: Sold by the workshop directly to a scrap dealer
options.C: Written off against the cancelled job in full
options.D: Returned by the workshop to the stores depot and taken back into stock, the job (Workshop Manufacturing Suspense) being credited with its value, so that only the material actually consumed is charged to the job

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, a specified number of items are reserved for exclusive purchase from Micro and Small Enterprises. The number of items so reserved is:

options.A: 108 items
options.B: 208 items
options.C: 358 items
options.D: 558 items

q: Advance payment of 98 per cent of the value of stores has been made to a supplier against the inspection certificate and despatch documents. On arrival at the destination depot, the entire consignment is rejected on inspection as not conforming to the specification. The advance payment made to the supplier is dealt with by:

options.A: Treating it as a final payment, the rejection being the Railway's own act
options.B: Recovering it from the personal pay of the depot storekeeper
options.C: Recovering it from the supplier, from his other bills, dues or security deposit with the Railway, in accordance with the contract
options.D: Booking it to the Stock Adjustment Account as a stores loss

q: Stores are purchased on 'F.O.R. despatching station' terms and a shortage occurs in transit before the consignment reaches the destination depot. In regard to the loss in transit, the correct position is that:

options.A: The risk in transit after despatch rests with the Railway as buyer under such terms, and its remedy lies in a claim on the carrier or under the transit insurance, and not on the supplier
options.B: The supplier must invariably make good the shortage free of cost, whatever the terms of purchase
options.C: The shortage is recovered from the pay of the consignee depot storekeeper
options.D: The shortage is ignored and the full despatched quantity is taken into stock

q: During a period, a depot received 50 demands for a stock item and was able to meet 46 of them in full from the stock in hand. The service level of the item for the period, measured as the proportion of demands met from stock, is:

options.A: 50 per cent
options.B: 46 per cent
options.C: 8 per cent
options.D: 92 per cent

q: In inventory control, the 'inventory position' of a stock item at any time means:

options.A: The quantity of the item physically present in the bins of the depot only
options.B: The stock in hand plus the quantities already on order (dues), as distinct from the stock in hand alone
options.C: The maximum level fixed for the item
options.D: The annual consumption of the item

q: During stock verification of coal stocked in a depot, a shortage is found which is within the permissible limits prescribed for normal losses of such stores in handling and transit. The shortage is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Recovering its full value from the stockholder in all cases
options.B: Treating the depot's entire coal stock as dead surplus
options.C: Adjusting it as a normal handling/transit loss under the sanction of the competent authority, without recovery from the stockholder, the loss being within the prescribed permissible limit
options.D: Concealing it by reducing the balances of another item in stock

q: Stores of the same item are issued from a depot in two different transactions: in the first, to a depot of another zonal railway, and in the second, to an outside party. The correct pricing of the two issues is:

options.A: To the other railway — at book value, settled by book adjustment between the railways; to the outside party — at book value plus the prescribed departmental charges, recovered in cash
options.B: To the other railway — at book value plus departmental charges; to the outside party — at book value only
options.C: In both cases — at the current market price on the date of issue
options.D: In both cases — free of cost, as both are Government bodies

q: An item is purchased by a depot on ex-works terms and the Railway pays the freight for its carriage to the depot separately. The freight so paid is treated in the priced accounts as:

options.A: A charge to be recovered from the depot storekeeper
options.B: A traffic earning of the Railway
options.C: A suspense item to be written off at the end of the year
options.D: A part of the cost of the stores, being taken into account in fixing the book (issue) rate of the item

q: A railway workshop manufactures a component and transfers it to a stores depot for stocking. In the accounts, the transfer is given effect by:

options.A: Debiting the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense and crediting the stores stock account
options.B: Debiting the stores stock account with the value of the component and crediting the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Making no entry until the component is issued to a consuming department
options.D: Debiting the component to the personal account of the Depot Materials Superintendent

q: A storekeeper, to save clerical work, posts the bin cards of his ward once a week in bulk from loose slips, instead of recording each receipt and issue as and when it takes place. This practice is objectionable mainly because:

options.A: Bin cards are required to be posted only by the Accounts Department
options.B: Weekly posting increases the price of the stores in stock
options.C: The custody accounts must reflect every receipt and issue contemporaneously, so that the balance on the bin card agrees with the physical stock at any time; bulk posting after a lapse of time defeats this check and invites errors and shortages remaining undetected
options.D: Loose slips are not permitted to be kept in a depot under any circumstances

q: The duplicate keys of the locks of the godowns and wards of a stores depot are, as a measure of safe custody, required to be:

options.A: Kept in a sealed cover in the custody of the officer in charge of the depot, for use in an emergency
options.B: Retained by the storekeeper along with the original keys
options.C: Deposited with the supplier who supplied the stores
options.D: Kept in an open tray at the depot gate

q: Verification of stores carried out when the charge of a depot is handed over from one stockholder to another differs from the periodical stock verification by the Accounts Department in that the former is carried out by:

options.A: The stock verifiers of the Accounts Department in all cases
options.B: The supplier of the stores in the depot
options.C: The Railway Protection Force
options.D: The incoming stockholder himself, who satisfies himself about the balances he is taking over, whereas periodical verification is carried out independently by the Accounts stock verifiers

q: Lubricating oil and tools and plant are both obtained from a stores depot, but their accounting after issue differs. The correct distinction is that:

options.A: Both are written off from all accounts at the time of issue
options.B: The oil remains on the Dead Stock Register, while the tools are consumed on issue
options.C: The oil, being a consumable store, is charged off on issue and is not required to be returned or accounted for thereafter, while the tools and plant, being returnable stores, remain borne on the Dead Stock Register and are accountable until they are returned or regularly condemned
options.D: The oil is borne on the Dead Stock Register, while the tools are charged off on issue

q: Costly and slow-moving stores items, such as insurance spares, which are required only occasionally, are stocked, instead of being stocked in every depot of a railway, at:

options.A: The depot nearest to the supplier's factory in all cases
options.B: A nominated depot, from which the requirements of the other depots served by it can be met, so that duplicate stocking of such items at many places is avoided
options.C: The headquarters office of the zonal railway
options.D: The workshop which last used the item

q: A depot holds a quantity of stores in perfectly serviceable condition, but the class of locomotives for which they were stocked has been withdrawn from service and the stores can no longer be used on the railway. Such stores are correctly treated as:

options.A: Obsolete stores, to be placed before the Survey Committee for condemnation and disposal, notwithstanding their serviceable physical condition
options.B: Vital stores, to be retained in stock permanently
options.C: Imprest stores of the loco shed
options.D: Stores in transit, to be shown under Purchase Suspense

q: A supplier's bill for stores, supported by the purchase order, the inspection note and the receipt note for the quantity received and accepted, is put up for payment. Which of the following is NOT a check exercised at the stage of passing the bill for payment?

options.A: That the rate charged in the bill agrees with the rate in the purchase order
options.B: That the quantity billed for does not exceed the quantity received and accepted as per the receipt note
options.C: That the arithmetical calculations in the bill are correct
options.D: That the consuming department really needed the stores, which is a matter examined at the stage of vetting of the indent before the purchase was made

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, where the value of a procurement exceeds Rs 10 crore, the local content claimed by a supplier is required to be supported by a certificate issued by:

options.A: The depot storekeeper receiving the stores
options.B: The supplier's own sales manager alone, in all cases
options.C: The statutory auditor (or, as prescribed, the cost auditor) of the supplier
options.D: The Inspector of Stores Accounts

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the stores balance of a railway?

options.A: Stores physically held in the depots of the railway
options.B: Stores in transit which have been paid for and are outstanding under Purchase Suspense
options.C: Stores already issued from depots to works and charged to the accounts of those works
options.D: Amounts recoverable for stores issued, outstanding under the stores suspense heads

q: A shortage of stores found in stock verification is adjusted in the first instance through the Stock Adjustment Account. Subsequently, the amount of the shortage is recovered from the stockholder, whose negligence was established. The amount so recovered is correctly accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting it to the Stock Adjustment Account, against the debit originally raised for the shortage
options.B: Retaining it in cash in the depot for petty expenses
options.C: Crediting it to the personal account of the stock verifier
options.D: Booking it as a fresh receipt of stores in the priced ledger

q: Two imprests held in a depot organisation — a cash imprest for petty expenses and a stores imprest held by a field official — are accounted for in different ways. The correct pairing is:

options.A: Cash imprest — by stores on hand plus consumption account; Stores imprest — by cash balance plus vouchers
options.B: Both imprests are accounted for only by the cash balance in hand
options.C: Both imprests are accounted for only by a narrative report of the stock verifier
options.D: Cash imprest — by the cash balance in hand plus the vouchers for expenditure incurred, making up the imprest amount; Stores imprest — by the stores physically on hand plus the account of stores consumed, making up the imprest quantity

q: A consuming department, instead of placing its demand on the stores depot, proposes to place a purchase order for stores directly on a firm of its own choice. The correct position is that:

options.A: Any department may purchase stores directly from any firm at its discretion
options.B: The department may do so only for stores required for resale to the public
options.C: Purchases of stores are arranged by the Stores Department on the demands/indents of the consuming departments, and direct purchase by a consuming department is permissible only where it is authorised, e.g. petty local purchases within the powers delegated for the purpose
options.D: The department may purchase directly only if the value exceeds Rs 1 crore

q: Which of the following will NOT, by itself, tend to increase the stores balance of a railway?

options.A: Providing coverage for stock items in excess of their actual requirements
options.B: Prompt survey and disposal of dead surplus and obsolete stock lying in depots
options.C: Accumulation of amounts paid for stores but not yet received, outstanding under Purchase Suspense
options.D: Continued stocking of slow-moving items for which demands have ceased

q: Two balances of a railway are under review. The first represents stores physically held in depots and borne in the priced stock accounts; the second represents amounts paid to suppliers for stores which have not yet been received. The two balances are represented respectively by:

options.A: Purchase Suspense — Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Sales Suspense — Purchase Suspense
options.C: Stores Suspense (stock account) — Purchase Suspense
options.D: Stock Adjustment Account — Sales Suspense

q: A depot receives material against a purchase order in March and takes it into stock, but the supplier's bill for it is received and paid only in April. At the close of March, the receipt of this material, unmatched by any payment, gives rise in the Purchase Suspense account to:

options.A: A credit, representing material received for which bills have not yet been paid
options.B: A debit, representing bills paid for which material has not been received
options.C: No entry at all, as Purchase Suspense is operated only on payment of bills
options.D: A debit to the Stock Adjustment Account for the value of the material

q: Item P has an annual consumption of 150 units at a book rate of Rs 1,200 per unit. Item Q has an annual consumption of 6,000 units at a book rate of Rs 25 per unit. For the purpose of ABC classification, the correct position is that:

options.A: Q ranks above P, because its annual consumption in units is much larger
options.B: P and Q rank equally, because both are stock items of the depot
options.C: Neither item can be classified until its maximum stock level is fixed
options.D: P ranks above Q, because the annual consumption value of P (Rs 1,80,000) exceeds that of Q (Rs 1,50,000), ABC classification being based on annual consumption value

q: Which of the following is NOT an element of the landed cost at which an imported stores item is taken into stock?

options.A: The invoice price of the item
options.B: The departmental charges added when stores are issued to an outside party
options.C: The freight paid for bringing the item to the depot
options.D: The customs duty paid on the item

q: During stock verification, a shortage of an item is found in one ward of a depot and an excess of a different item is found in another ward of the same depot. The correct treatment of the two differences is that:

options.A: The excess is set off against the shortage, as both differences belong to the same depot
options.B: Both differences are ignored, as they cancel each other in value
options.C: Each difference is recorded and adjusted separately through the Stock Adjustment Account, a shortage of one item not being set off against an excess of a different item
options.D: The stockholder is given credit for the excess against the shortage as a matter of course

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 9,600 units. The stock in hand is 1,250 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 350 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 2 months
options.B: 1 month
options.C: 4 months
options.D: 6 months

q: A tenderer whose offer was not accepted in a stores tender demands refund of the 'security deposit' furnished by him. The correct position is that:

options.A: The amount he furnished is refunded as security deposit in all cases
options.B: No amount furnished by any tenderer is ever refundable
options.C: The amount can be refunded only after the stores are supplied by the successful tenderer
options.D: An unsuccessful tenderer furnishes only Earnest Money Deposit with his tender, which is refundable to him; Security Deposit is furnished only by the successful tenderer after acceptance of his tender

q: Scrap lying in a depot is put up for sale, and in a separate proceeding the purchase office buys stores from tenderers whose offers have been found technically acceptable. The correct pairing of the two proceedings is:

options.A: Scrap sale — reverse auction, in which bids move downward; Stores purchase — e-auction, in which bids move upward
options.B: Both proceedings are conducted as reverse auctions on IREPS
options.C: Scrap sale — e-auction, in which successive bids move upward; Stores purchase — reverse auction, in which successive bids move downward
options.D: Both proceedings are conducted as e-auctions on IREPS

q: A stores contract provides for liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay, as stipulated in the contract. Stores of the value of Rs 2,40,000 are supplied 17 days late, the part of a week counting as a full week as stipulated. The liquidated damages leviable are:
Which of the following is NOT a function of the stock verifier of the Accounts Department during stock verification of a depot?

options.A: Physically verifying the stores with the book balances
options.B: Preparing a stock sheet for the differences found between the physical and book balances
options.C: Bringing out procedural irregularities noticed during verification through a narrative report
options.D: Sanctioning the write-off of the value of stores found short during his verification

q: A fire breaks out in a depot godown despite all prescribed precautions having been taken by the stockholder, and a quantity of stores is destroyed. After due enquiry into the loss, the correct position regarding the stockholder is that:

options.A: He must make good the full value of the stores destroyed, in all cases of fire
options.B: He is not held personally liable for the loss, it having occurred despite the exercise of due care and precaution on his part, and the loss is dealt with under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: The destroyed stores are treated as dead surplus and sold by e-auction
options.D: The value of the destroyed stores is recovered from the stock verifier of the depot

q: A stock item has a safety (buffer) stock of 250 units and an Economic Order Quantity of 800 units. Immediately after a fresh receipt of the Economic Order Quantity is taken into stock, the stock of the item, consumption having in the meantime drawn only on the cycle stock in the normal course, will be at its maximum of:

options.A: 250 units
options.B: 800 units
options.C: 1,050 units
options.D: 550 units

q: Paints, cement and similar stores which deteriorate on exposure to weather are received at a depot which has both open yard space and covered sheds. As a measure of proper storage and preservation, such stores are correctly stocked:

options.A: Under covered sheds, protected from weather, rather than in the open yard
options.B: In the open yard, exposure to weather having no effect on such stores
options.C: Along with inflammable stores in the same godown in all cases
options.D: In the wagons in which they arrived, until they are issued

q: A lorry driver presents himself at the gate of a stores depot to take out a consignment of scrap, producing only a copy of the bin card of the item and a verbal message from a depot clerk. The gate staff act correctly in:

options.A: Allowing the consignment out, the bin card being sufficient authority
options.B: Allowing the consignment out against the verbal message, noting it in the gate register
options.C: Handing over the consignment against a receipt taken from the driver alone
options.D: Refusing to allow the material out of the depot until a gate pass, issued on the basis of the delivery order for the scrap sold, is produced

q: A depot holds 600 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 30 per unit. It issues 200 units, and thereafter receives a fresh lot of 400 units taken into stock at Rs 45 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item after the fresh receipt is:

options.A: Rs 45 per unit
options.B: Rs 37.50 per unit
options.C: Rs 30 per unit
options.D: Rs 40 per unit

q: A stock item has a safety stock of 400 units and an Economic Order Quantity of 1,000 units, the inventory being held, on the average, at the safety stock plus half the Economic Order Quantity. The inventory carrying cost is Rs 12 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost of the average inventory of the item is:
Which of the following is NOT, by itself, a ground for rejecting a stores tender?

options.A: The tender is received after the due date and time fixed for its receipt
options.B: The tender contains a material deviation from the conditions of tender stipulated by the Railway
options.C: The tenderer is a Micro or Small Enterprise participating in the tender
options.D: The tenderers are found to have formed a cartel and quoted collusive rates

q: During stock verification of oils held in a depot, a shortage is found which exceeds the permissible limit prescribed for normal losses of such stores in handling and transit. The correct treatment of the shortage is that:

options.A: The entire shortage is treated as a normal handling loss in all cases
options.B: The entire coal and oil stock of the depot is declared dead surplus
options.C: The shortage is concealed by reducing the balance of another oil item
options.D: Only the shortage within the prescribed permissible limit is treated as a normal loss; the excess beyond that limit is enquired into and dealt with by recovery or adjustment under the sanction of the competent authority

q: During a year, the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is debited with Rs 3,20,000 on account of shortages and downward revisions of book rates, and credited with Rs 1,45,000 on account of excesses found in stock verification. The net balance of the account for the year is:

options.A: A credit balance of Rs 1,75,000
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 1,75,000
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 4,65,000
options.D: Nil, the debits and credits being written off against each other in full

q: The priced ledger balances of a depot do not agree with the balance under Stores Suspense in the General Books of the railway. The disagreement is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Reconciling the priced ledger balances with the General Books balance periodically, investigating the differences so brought out and rectifying the postings responsible for them
options.B: Altering the General Books balance to agree with the priced ledger without any investigation
options.C: Writing off the whole difference to the Stock Adjustment Account at once, without enquiry
options.D: Closing the priced ledger of the depot and opening a fresh ledger

q: On the same day, a depot issues stores of the same total value to two destinations: a manufacturing job in hand in a railway workshop, and a revenue (working expense) head of a consuming department. The correct debit of the two issues is:

options.A: Both issues are debited to the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: Both issues are debited to the revenue head under Primary Unit 27
options.C: The workshop issue is debited to the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, to be charged to the job; the revenue issue is debited to the revenue head of the consuming department, stores issues to revenue being linked to Primary Unit 27
options.D: Both issues are debited to Purchase Suspense until the end of the year

q: Which of the following is NOT a stage in the disposal of unserviceable stores as scrap?

options.A: Examination of the stores by a Survey Committee and their condemnation
options.B: Formation of the condemned stores into lots and their inclusion in an auction catalogue
options.C: Sale of the lots by e-auction to the highest bidder
options.D: Issue of the condemned stores to a consuming department at the book rate for regular use

q: A depot issues 180 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 220 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 10 per cent of the book value, as given in the conditions of issue. The total amount recoverable from the outside party is:

Material supplied by a firm is rejected on inspection at a depot, and the firm thereafter supplies replacement material against the same purchase order. Before the replacement material is taken into stock, the depot acts correctly in:

options.A: Getting the replacement material inspected and accepted, and taking it into stock only thereafter under a receipt note
options.B: Taking the replacement material straight into stock without inspection, the original lot having already been inspected once
options.C: Issuing the replacement material directly to the consuming department without any receipt entry
options.D: Refusing the replacement material in every case and cancelling the purchase order at once

q: The Purchase Suspense account of a railway opens with a credit balance of Rs 6 lakh. During the month, bills amounting to Rs 28 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 31 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance of the account is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.B: A credit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 9 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 9 lakh

q: Two consignments of imported stores are under despatch to a railway, one purchased on F.O.B. terms and the other on C.I.F. terms. The correct distinction between the two purchases is that:

options.A: Under both terms, the marine insurance of the consignment is arranged by the foreign supplier
options.B: Under C.I.F. terms, the buyer arranges the marine insurance, the price covering only the cost of the goods
options.C: Under F.O.B. terms, the price includes the cost, insurance and freight up to the destination port
options.D: Under F.O.B. terms, the price covers the cost of the goods put on board the ship and the marine insurance is arranged by the Railway as buyer, whereas under C.I.F. terms the price itself includes the cost, the insurance and the freight

q: An item is stocked in a depot for the first time and there is no past record of its consumption in the depot. Its Average Annual Consumption (AAC) is fixed, in such a case, on the basis of:

options.A: The estimated requirements of the item anticipated from the consuming departments, there being no consumption history to go by
options.B: The AAC of a different item of roughly the same book rate
options.C: The quantity of the item held by the supplier in his godown
options.D: A figure equal to the maximum stock level of the depot as a whole

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the cost of ordering stores?

options.A: The cost of preparing and placing the purchase order on the supplier
options.B: The insurance premium paid for insuring the stock held in the depot against fire and theft risks in storage
options.C: The cost of progressing (following up) the purchase order with the supplier
options.D: The cost of receiving and inspecting the stores on their arrival at the depot

q: The annual requirement of an item is 1,250 units and its Economic Order Quantity, as given, is 250 units. The cost of placing one order, as given, is Rs 100. The total ordering cost incurred during the year is:

options.A: Rs 100
options.C: Rs 500

q: Stores are transferred from one depot to another depot of the same zonal railway. The correct accounting and pricing of the transfer is that the stores are:

options.A: Priced at book value plus departmental charges and the amount recovered in cash from the receiving depot
options.B: Treated as a sale to an outside party and settled through Sales Suspense
options.C: Written off in the despatching depot and taken afresh on charge in the receiving depot at market price
options.D: Priced at the book rate, without addition of departmental charges, the value being adjusted in the accounts of the same railway on the basis of the transfer documents

q: A depot holds 900 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 58 to Rs 50 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

After the opening of a stores tender but before the expiry of the period of validity of his offer, a tenderer withdraws his tender and demands refund of the Earnest Money Deposit furnished by him. The correct position is that:

options.A: The Earnest Money Deposit is refunded to him in full as a matter of course
options.B: The Earnest Money Deposit is liable to be forfeited, the tender having been withdrawn during the period of validity of the offer
options.C: The tenderer is given a fresh tender to submit in place of the withdrawn tender
options.D: The withdrawal has no consequence and the tender is treated as still subsisting

q: Two actions against a supplier firm are under consideration in a purchase office: holding business dealings with the firm in abeyance pending completion of an enquiry against it, and a formal order debarring the firm from dealings after it has been given an opportunity to show cause. The two actions are respectively:

options.A: Banning of the firm — Suspension of business dealings
options.B: Blacklisting for all Government departments — Local purchase
options.C: Suspension of business dealings — Banning of the firm
options.D: Risk purchase — Suspension of business dealings

q: Five wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 2 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 900 per wagon per day, as given. The total demurrage payable is:

options.A: Rs 900

q: A depot issues stores for a deposit work, i.e. a work executed by the Railway on behalf of an outside party at that party's cost. The depot at first debits the value of the stores to its own revenue (working expense) head. This debit is objectionable because the value of stores issued for a deposit work is correctly:

options.A: Debited to the account of the deposit work itself, so that its cost is recovered from the outside party at whose cost the work is executed
options.B: Debited to the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in all cases
options.C: Written off as a stores loss at the end of the year
options.D: Debited to Purchase Suspense until the work is completed

q: A costly item of equipment ordered by the Railways is under manufacture at the supplier's works over a long period, and the inspecting authority examines the work at successive stages of its manufacture itself, instead of inspecting only the finished product. Such inspection is known as:

options.A: Receipt inspection at the destination depot
options.B: Stage inspection, carried out in stages during the process of manufacture
options.C: Surprise verification of stores in the depot
options.D: Stock verification by the Accounts Department

q: During a period, a depot receives 80 demands for a stock item and is able to meet 68 of them in full from the stock in hand, the remaining demands being cases of stock-out. The service level of the item for the period is:

options.A: 80 per cent
options.B: 68 per cent
options.C: 85 per cent
options.D: 15 per cent

q: Which of the following is NOT an object served by the codification of stores items through Price Ledger (PL) numbers?

options.A: Identifying each stores item uniquely in all the depots of the railway
options.B: Facilitating computerised inventory control of stores
options.C: Preventing the same item being stocked under different names in different depots
options.D: Selecting the supplier from whom a stores item is to be purchased

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a 'B' category stock item of a depot is sent by the depot to Headquarters Finance for vetting. After the model SOP of 2018, this reference is unnecessary because:

options.A: Vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is required only for 'A' category items, the AAC of 'B' and 'C' category items being fixed at the railway/depot level itself
options.B: The AAC of 'B' category items is vetted by the supplier supplying the item
options.C: No AAC is required to be fixed for 'B' category items at all
options.D: The AAC of all categories of items is vetted by Headquarters Finance without exception

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 55 units per day and the lead time for its emergency procurement, as given, is 4 days. The danger level of the item is:

options.A: 55 units
options.B: 220 units
options.C: 110 units
options.D: 440 units

q: A purchase officer proposes to make a risk purchase against a defaulting supplier straightaway, without any action on the original purchase order. This course is irregular because, before a risk purchase is effected, the Railway is required to:

options.A: Place a fresh open tender for the entire annual requirement of the item
options.B: Obtain a fresh Proprietary Article Certificate for the item in all cases
options.C: Cancel the original purchase order in respect of the quantity in default and give due notice of the risk purchase to the defaulting supplier
options.D: Insure the stores to be risk-purchased with a commercial insurer

q: A non-stock item purchased against the specific demand of a work is received at a depot. The correct accounting of the item on its receipt is that it is:

options.A: Taken into the priced stock of the depot and stocked like any other stock item
options.B: Borne on the Dead Stock Register of the depot permanently
options.C: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account on receipt
options.D: Not taken into stock, but charged direct to the account of the work or department which demanded it, the item having been procured for that specific demand

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 42 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.58 crore and the closing balance is Rs 50 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 1.50 crore
options.B: Rs 2.00 crore
options.C: Rs 50 lakh
options.D: Rs 2.50 crore

q: A storekeeper mixes unserviceable stores, which are awaiting survey and disposal, with the serviceable stock of the same items in his ward. This practice is objectionable mainly because such unserviceable stores are required to be:

options.A: Issued to consuming departments along with the serviceable stock
options.B: Kept separately, segregated from the serviceable stock, until they are surveyed, condemned and disposed of
options.C: Taken into the priced stock at an enhanced book rate
options.D: Returned to the suppliers who originally supplied them in all cases

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 90 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 3 crore. The Turnover Ratio of the stores is:

The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 60 lakh, the receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.40 crore and the closing balance is Rs 75 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:

options.A: Rs 2.25 crore
options.B: Rs 1.50 crore
options.C: Rs 3.00 crore
options.D: Rs 75 lakh

q: The annual consumption of an item is 2,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 40 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:

options.A: 100 units
options.B: 400 units
options.C: 200 units
options.D: 283 units

q: The annual requirement of an item is 2,400 units and its Economic Order Quantity, as given, is 300 units. The cost of placing one order, as given, is Rs 120. The total ordering cost incurred during the year is:

options.A: Rs 960
options.B: Rs 120
options.D: Rs 300

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 900 units. Its average consumption is 40 units per day and the average lead time is 15 days. The minimum level of the item is:

options.A: 600 units
options.B: 1,500 units
options.C: 900 units
options.D: 300 units

q: The re-order level of a stock item is 700 units and its re-order quantity is 900 units. The minimum consumption of the item is 15 units per day and the minimum lead period is 10 days. The maximum level of the item is:

options.A: 1,600 units
options.B: 1,450 units
options.C: 1,750 units
options.D: 1,300 units

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 7,200 units. The stock in hand is 1,500 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 2 months
options.B: 6 months
options.C: 3 months
options.D: 4 months

q: The Average Annual Consumption (AAC) of a stock item is 6,000 units and coverage for four months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 650 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 350 units. The quantity required to be ordered is:

options.A: 2,000 units
options.B: 650 units
options.C: 1,350 units
options.D: 1,000 units

q: A depot holds 300 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 40 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 55 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item after the fresh receipt is:

options.A: Rs 46 per unit
options.B: Rs 55 per unit
options.C: Rs 47.50 per unit
options.D: Rs 40 per unit

q: A depot holds 800 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 35 to Rs 42 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:

options.A: A debit of Rs 5,600 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: A credit of Rs 5,600 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: A credit of Rs 33,600 to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: A debit of Rs 28,000 to the Stock Adjustment Account
